mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 5%, it may indicate monetary tightening, leading to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods after FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both real estate investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following increased RSAFS and HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following increased INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% may stimulate economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following FEDFUNDS below 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following significant PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong economic demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following increased GDPC1 and HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% may indicate inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following increased CPIAUCSL, the hypothesis is rejected.
